items.name: cylinder_count
items.description: Number of cylinders. 1..4 is the supported product range; the engine core contains no per-engine code, only this number and the geometry below.

items.name: rod_ratio
items.description: Connecting rod length / crank radius. Not published for the GT650; it only affects the pumping-loss and volumetric-efficiency model, so a conservative value is safe. Register UNK-GT-019.

items.name: cycle_teeth
items.description: Engine cycle. 720 degrees is the only four-stroke timing model implemented.

items.name: crank_layout
items.description: Crank arrangement. Determines the firing angles used by the scheduler.

items.name: firing_order_cyl0
items.description: Which physical cylinder fires first. Wrong values inject into an exhaust stroke, so this is gated by the arming check and verified on the bench. Register UNK-GT-003.

items.name: custom_firing_angle_0
items.description: Firing angle of cylinder 0 after its TDC, for crank_layout = custom.

items.name: cam_phase_offset_deg
items.description: Crank angle of the cam reference edge relative to cylinder 1 TDC. Without a measured value the configuration must not allow sequential operation. Register UNK-GT-002.

items.name: max_rpm
items.description: Design maximum. The hard limiter uses the safety copy, not this value; this is used for table axis scaling and for plausibility rejection.

items.name: fuel_ethanol_fraction
items.description: Ethanol fraction of the current fuel, from a flex-fuel sensor or set by hand. Drives stoich AFR, density, cold start, ignition blend and lambda target.

items.name: fuel_stoich_afr_gasoline
items.description: Stoich air/fuel ratio for pump gasoline (14.7:1).

items.name: fuel_stoich_afr_ethanol
items.description: Stoich AFR for pure ethanol (about 9.0:1).

items.name: air_density_sea_level
items.description: Dry air density at 15 C, 101.325 kPa. Reference for the barometric correction.

items.name: displacement_cc
items.description: Optional: a stated total displacement, cross-checked against bore x stroke at configuration load. A disagreement beyond 2 percent refuses the configuration rather than being quietly preferred. Leave at 0 to derive it purely.

items.name: profile_crank
items.description: Crank trigger wheel profile. The generic profiles cover the common aftermarket wheels; anything else is defined by the explicit profile items below. Register UNK-GT-001.

items.name: teeth
items.description: Teeth per revolution on this wheel (counted as if none were missing).

items.name: missing_teeth
items.description: Size of the contiguous missing-tooth gap, in teeth.

items.name: teeth_per_rev
items.description: 1 for a crank wheel, 2 for a half-speed cam wheel.

items.name: tooth1_angle_atdc
items.description: Crank angle after TDC at which tooth 1 passes the sensor. This is the single most consequential number in the product; it must be established with a timing light, not guessed.

items.name: input_filter_level
items.description: Software input filter, 0 off .. 3 aggressive. Default is deliberately mild: a rejected real tooth desynchronises phase, which is worse than accepting one noise edge. Rejection count is a logged channel.

items.name: sync_skip_revolutions
items.description: Revolutions of confirmation required before sync is declared.

items.name: min_period_us
items.description: Shortest plausible tooth period. Edges faster than this are rejected, which is what makes an impossible period and overspeed detectable. Register UNK-FW-001.

items.name: max_period_us
items.description: Longest plausible period before a tooth timeout and SYNC_LOST.

items.name: overspeed_period_us
items.description: Below this period the decoder declares a hard fault and inhibits output.

items.name: prediction_enabled
items.description: Predict the rate at the target angle from the measured acceleration, bounded. Disabling it makes timing exact only at constant speed and is for bench work.

items.name: max_accel_rpm_per_s
items.description: Acceleration bound for the predictor. Beyond it, prediction is disabled for the window and a diagnostic is counted. No unbounded extrapolation is permitted.

items.name: cam_teeth
items.description: Cam wheel tooth count, used when profile_cam is 'custom'. The named profiles carry their own count and ignore this item, because a 4-tooth half-speed wheel decoded as 3 teeth produces a cam phase that is wrong by a quarter of a cam revolution - and a wrong cam phase under sequential injection is a cylinder fired at the wrong time, which is not a starting problem, it is a broken-engine problem.

items.name: cam_missing_teeth
items.description: Gap teeth on a custom cam wheel, counted from tooth 1. A cam wheel with no gap has no phase reference, so the decoder cannot tell one cam revolution from the next and sequential injection is refused rather than guessed.

items.name: tps1_slope
items.description: Throttle opening per volt at the sensor pins. 20 %/V is a 0..5 V sensor; 25 %/V is the 0.5..4.5 V form, which leaves a live diagnostic band at each stop. Register UNK-GT-007 - the fitted sensor is not yet known.

items.name: tps1_min
items.description: Lower plausibility bound, deliberately a little below the closed stop so a real idle position is not rejected as RANGE on every cycle.

items.name: tps1_max
items.description: Upper plausibility bound, the throttle stop plus margin.

items.name: tps1_rate_limit
items.description: Open-loop rate limiter, not a smoothing filter: RATE_LIMIT is a reported flag so a genuine fast transient stays distinguishable from a limited one (test S13).

items.name: tps1_transfer
items.description: Transfer-function family for this channel (SENS-001 sec.3). ratiometric divides the code by the ADC full scale and scales by the *measured* 5 V reference, so a drifting sensor rail cannot quietly rescale the throttle.

items.name: tps1_fault_behaviour
items.description: What the control loop does when this channel is invalid. The choice is a deliberate calibration per the fail-operational / fail-safe split in SC-001 sec.4, never an accidental default.

items.name: map_slope
items.description: Pressure per volt. 200 kPa/V spans 0..1000 kPa absolute over 0..5 V, which covers both a 2-bar and a 3-bar gauge. Register UNK-GT-008 - the fitted sensor is unknown, and a 4-bar part needs a different slope.

items.name: map_min
items.description: Lower plausibility bound in absolute terms. A negative band is admitted so a gauge briefly below its zero on a cold start is not a fault.

items.name: map_max
items.description: Upper plausibility bound. Must not be set below the boost target.

items.name: map_rate_limit
items.description: Shared with the transient model. A value clipped here is otherwise indistinguishable from a real pressure event, so the limiter is always flagged.

items.name: map_fault_behaviour
items.description: Speed density has a declared degraded path, so the default is the limp: with MAP invalid the load estimator falls to the alternate strategy and records the substitution in the correction vector (FUEL-001 sec.2).

items.name: maf_slope
items.description: Air mass flow per volt at the pins. Only relevant when the MAF fuel strategy is selected; a motorcycle normally has no MAF, and an absent sensor is declared by transfer = none rather than by leaving a plausible number behind.

items.name: maf_max
items.description: Upper plausibility bound; must exceed idle flow with a margin.

items.name: maf_fault_behaviour
items.description: MAF is the only absolute air measurement, so losing it changes the *nature* of the calculation; the declared behaviour is to switch load strategy, not to continue with a held value.

items.name: ect_slope
items.description: Linearised front-end gain of the coolant thermistor. Negative, because an NTC on a pull-up reads lower as it heats. With transfer = ntc_table the Steinhart-Hart coefficients from the sensor profile take precedence and this pair is the linearisation seed. Register UNK-GT-009.

items.name: ect_min
items.description: Lower plausibility bound. It must not be set so high that a genuinely cold engine is reported RANGE and loses cold-start enrichment.

items.name: ect_fault_behaviour
items.description: A coolant sensor failure does not stop a running engine; it substitutes a conservative warm value and requests service. Running on a fixed enrichment value after losing coolant is how an engine is destroyed, so the fallback is warm, never cold.

items.name: iat_slope
items.description: Linearised front-end gain of the intake thermistor. Register UNK-GT-009 covers the curve. IAT drives charge-temperature ignition correction and the ethanol charge-cooling term, so a wrong slope is a persistent timing error rather than a small display error.

items.name: oil_pressure_slope
items.description: Oil pressure per volt; 2 bar/V is the common 0..5 V / 0..10 bar sender. A switch instead of a sender is the other possibility, and it is declared by choosing transfer = switch_hysteresis rather than by guessing a slope. Register UNK-GT-018.

items.name: oil_pressure_min
items.description: Lower plausibility bound; a small negative band absorbs sender zero error.

items.name: oil_pressure_fault_behaviour
items.description: Oil starvation is a latching, escalating hazard (SC-001 H-08). The declared action here only decides between substituting a value and entering the limp; the action taken is the safety group's latching cut with recovery hysteresis.

items.name: oil_temp_max
items.description: Upper plausibility bound; oil above this is a failure, not a reading.

items.name: fuel_pressure_slope
items.description: Rail pressure per volt at the sensor. Distinct from the pressure-compensation slope in the fuel group: this one turns volts into bars, that one corrects the delivered mass. Register UNK-GT-005.

items.name: fuel_pressure_fault_behaviour
items.description: A lost pressure sensor must not mean a rich engine. The declared fallback is the conservative nominal pressure, and the low-pressure protection in the safety group is what actually restricts fuel.

items.name: egt_slope
items.description: Degrees per volt at the amplifier output. A Type-K front end is about 41.9 uV per degree, so the amplifier gain sets this; 167 degC/V spans 0..835 C over 0..5 V. Probe placement matters far more than the gain and is not yet known.

items.name: egt_max
items.description: Upper plausibility bound. EGT is a diagnostic input, not a control input, so this band may be generous; the protective limit is safety.egt_max_c.

items.name: ethanol_slope
items.description: Ethanol fraction per volt; 0.2/V is a 0..5 V linear sensor, and most real flex sensors are 50..500 Hz, selected by transfer. Most motorcycles have no flex sensor at all, which is transfer = none with engine.fuel_ethanol_fraction set by hand instead.

items.name: ethanol_rate_limit
items.description: Deliberately slow. Fuel does not change blend, so a fast transition is a sensor fault and must be rejected outright rather than blended through, which would smear a real disagreement into an undetectable wrong value.

items.name: ethanol_fault_behaviour
items.description: Hold the last plausible blend for a bounded time instead of reverting at once: refuelling with a different blend genuinely happens mid-ride, and an instant step back to pure gasoline would itself be a large fuelling error.

items.name: battery_slope
items.description: Divider ratio of the battery-sense input: 3.0 means a 12 V pack presents 3.0 V to the ADC. Battery voltage feeds injector dead time, coil dwell capability and both under- and over-voltage protections, so a wrong ratio is a whole-vehicle fuelling and timing error rather than a gauge error.

items.name: battery_max
items.description: Upper plausibility bound; above this the reading is a wiring fault.

items.name: battery_fault_behaviour
items.description: The default is the limp. With no battery measurement the ECU cannot know whether the coils are reaching primary current, so it widens no pulse and reduces authority instead of guessing.

items.name: ref5v_slope
items.description: Ratio of the monitored sensor rail to the ADC reading, 1.0 for a plain divider. This channel measures the rail; it never drives it (IOM-001 AI_5V_REF).

items.name: ref5v_min
items.description: Lower bound of the sensor-rail tolerance. This item is essential, and it is the least obvious channel in the product: if the 5 V rail collapses, every 5 V sensor - throttle, MAP, MAF, lambda, fuel and oil pressure, ethanol, EGT - reads incorrectly AND plausibly, so the per-channel open/short, range and rate checks are all fooled simultaneously. Monitoring the reference is the only way to detect that class of failure at all. Sensor test S9; IOM-001 sec.2.

items.name: ref5v_max
items.description: Upper bound of the sensor-rail tolerance, same argument as ref5v_min.

items.name: ref5v_fault_behaviour
items.description: Default 6 (invalidate_dependents) is not a tuning preference. A rail fault invalidates every ratiometric channel at the same instant, which is the NO_REFERENCE reason code in the SENS-001 sec.2 fault taxonomy.

items.name: lambda1_slope
items.description: Lambda per volt on the wideband controller's analogue output. The controller linearises the sensor; the ECU never interprets raw sensor volts. Register UNK-GT-010 - neither the fitting nor the controller type is known yet.

items.name: lambda1_freshness_ms
items.source_ref: SENS-001 sec.7 (lambda 40 ms in closed loop)

items.name: lambda1_fault_behaviour
items.description: An unready, failed or unplugged lambda sensor must never leave the closed loop running on the last value, so the declared behaviour is to mark it invalid and drop to the declared open-loop strategy (FUEL-001 test F12).

items.name: lambda2_slope
items.description: Second channel. Only populate this block when hardware_lambda_channel_count actually reports a second physical fitting; an unpopulated channel must be declared with transfer = none, not left at a plausible default.

items.name: lambda2_freshness_ms
items.source_ref: SENS-001 sec.7 (lambda 40 ms in closed loop)

items.name: lambda2_transfer
items.description: Defaults to none - a motorcycle with one exhaust fitting has one sensor.

items.name: lambda3_slope
items.description: Third channel, used for a 3- or 4-cylinder build with real per-cylinder fittings.

items.name: lambda3_freshness_ms
items.source_ref: SENS-001 sec.7 (lambda 40 ms in closed loop)

items.name: lambda4_slope
items.description: Fourth channel, for a 4-cylinder build with one fitting per cylinder.

items.name: lambda4_freshness_ms
items.source_ref: SENS-001 sec.7 (lambda 40 ms in closed loop)

items.name: sensor_filter_cutoff_hz
items.description: Default analogue anti-alias cutoff for the slow-changing channels. The fast channels (knock, ignition current, injector current) are deliberately excluded - their bandwidth is part of the signal, not noise.

items.name: sensor_dual_check_enabled
items.description: Cross-check a redundant pair (TPS1/TPS2, front/rear wheel). Enabled by default because the check costs nothing and a disagreement is otherwise invisible.

items.name: sensor_dual_mismatch_max
items.description: Largest disagreement between the two members of a pair, in percent of full scale. Above this the pair is declared INCONSISTENT (SENS-001 sec.8).

items.name: sensor_dual_policy
items.description: What happens on INCONSISTENT. The policy is explicit per configuration because "average the two" is only defensible for a cable throttle; for fly-by-wire, invalidating both is the honest answer.

items.name: sensor_frozen_window_ms
items.description: Window over which an unchanging value is declared FROZEN. Computed from a sequence advance and a timestamp, never from "the value looks plausible" (SENS-001 sec.1, hazard H-11).

items.name: sensor_reference_5v_enabled
items.description: The 5 V reference monitor. There is no safe default of off: without it, a collapsed sensor rail is undetectable and every ratiometric channel is simultaneously wrong in a plausible direction.

items.name: sensor_reference_5v_fault_action
items.description: What a reference fault does to the channels that depend on it. The default invalidates them, because continuing on untrusted rails is precisely the failure this channel exists to catch.

items.name: injector_driver_type
items.description: Injector power stage. Peak-and-hold exists only where a driver provides a bounded peak phase and a bounded hold phase; with a high-Z saturated driver the ECU must command a much longer pulse for the same flow. Register UNK-GT-004.

items.name: ignition_driver_topology
items.description: Coil topology, which determines whether the ECU computes dwell at all. A CDI is explicitly not assumed and is not supported without a validated profile entry (IGN-001 sec.1). Register UNK-GT-006.

items.name: injector_peak_current_a
items.description: Peak current the driver sources during the opening phase. Ignored for a high-Z saturated driver, which has no peak phase.

items.name: injector_hold_current_a
items.description: Hold current after opening. This is what keeps the driver's dissipation manageable over a long pulse; it is also the number that must be inside the driver IC's own limit, which is enforced in hardware.

items.name: injector_max_duty_pct
items.description: Hardware duty ceiling for the injector channels. Enforced by the driver, not only by software: exceeding it is a DTC and a protective cut, never a warning (ACT-001 sec.1, hazard H-04). The safety group carries the ECU-side ceiling.

items.name: ignition_peak_current_a
items.description: Primary current the gate stage sources while the coil charges. Sets how fast the coil reaches saturation and therefore how short the effective dwell has to be at high rpm.

items.name: ignition_hold_current_a
items.description: Current held after saturation. Keeping the coil saturated while the spark event is required is what a smart driver does automatically; with a dumb coil the ECU must stop the charge at the right instant.

items.name: ignition_max_dwell_ms
items.description: Hardware maximum dwell, enforced by a timer or by the smart driver independently of the CPU. This is a hardware property, not a software promise: with the CPU halted mid-dwell the timer still ends it (hazard H-03, test I3).

items.name: ignition_spark_divider_ratio
items.description: Primary-side divider ratio used for spark-duration feedback, which turns "we commanded a spark" into "a spark event was observed". That measured event is what the safety case and the dyno analyser actually need. Register UNK-HW-006.

items.name: aux_output_function_0
items.description: Function assigned to user output 0. Assignment is validated: two functions on one channel, or a function the hardware profile cannot support, is refused with a specific reason (ACT-001 sec.7).

items.name: aux_output_timeout_ms
items.description: Maximum continuous ON time for one aux output, after which the driver forces it off. No output in the product has an unbounded energised duration: a solenoid welded closed is a fire, and a stepper energised forever is a thermal event (ACT-001 sec.6, test A11).

items.name: aux_output_duty_max_pct
items.description: Duty ceiling for the PWM aux outputs, per output profile.

items.name: aux_output_flags
items.description: Per-output behaviour flags. The default sets failsafe_off, so with the ECU unpowered or wedged every aux output is off - the only state that is unambiguously safe for an unknown device attached to it.

items.name: hardware_capabilities
items.description: Capability set the firmware may assume. Derived from the hardware profile and the end-of-line test record, never hand-set: a capability is on only if the physical resource exists and passed end of line against the unit's serial number (IOM-001 sec.6). The remaining profile capabilities (CAN-FD, stepper IAC, anti-lag, internal log, spark feedback, injector diagnostics, gear and clutch sensing) live in the hardware profile binary.

items.name: hardware_fuel_pump_max_duty_pct
items.description: Duty ceiling for the pump drive. A short circuit latches the output off with a bounded retry policy, so the pump is a stopped engine rather than a melted harness. Register UNK-GT-012.

items.name: hardware_fuel_pump_timeout_ms
items.description: Maximum continuous pump ON time with a defined consequence, so a welded relay feedback contact cannot leave a pump running indefinitely.

items.name: hardware_main_relay_feedback
items.description: True when the main relay is actually monitored. A welded main relay is a common failure; without feedback the ECU can only report that it commanded the relay, which is not the same statement.

items.name: hardware_lambda_channel_count
items.description: Physical wideband input count. The controller refuses per-cylinder trim beyond this number, so it cannot imply a per-cylinder measurement that does not exist.

items.name: hardware_knock_channel_count
items.description: Physical knock inputs. Zero by default because no knock sensor is known to be fitted on this engine: knock detection is impossible without one, and no claim is made without hardware (IGN-001 sec.5). Register UNK-FW-008.

items.name: hardware_injector_channel_count
items.description: Physical injector output count, primary plus secondary. live_edit false.

items.name: hardware_ignition_channel_count
items.description: Physical ignition output count. live_edit false.

items.name: hardware_driver_overtemp_c
items.description: Driver overtemperature threshold at which the stage shuts down and raises a DTC, recovering after cooldown rather than latching (ACT-001 test A5).

items.name: hardware_stepper_max_energised_ms
items.description: Hard stall/timeout limit for the idle stepper. A stepper commanded forever is a thermal event, so the maximum energised time is bounded and a return-to-zero policy follows it.

items.name: hardware_wasted_spark_pairs
items.description: Number of wasted-spark coil pairs, which determines the correct pairing and polarity of the ignition outputs on a 4-cylinder build (IGN-001 test I11).

items.name: hardware_aux_output_count
items.description: Number of assignable user outputs exposed by this profile. live_edit false.

items.name: injector_flow_cc_per_s
items.description: Static flow rate at the reference pressure below. This is a *measured* number in a finished product (bench flow test or datasheet); until then it is an unverified placeholder and the ECU says so. Register UNK-GT-004.

items.name: injector_reference_pressure_kpa
items.description: The pressure at which injector_flow_cc_per_s was measured. Flow and pressure are meaningless apart: quoting one without the other is a hidden calibration.

items.name: injector_dead_time_ms
items.description: Dead time at the nominal battery voltage: the pulse that opens the injector but delivers no measurable fuel. Must be strictly less than the minimum pulse, and a real dead-time curve is monotonic in battery voltage (test F1).

items.name: injector_min_pulse_ms
items.description: Smallest pulse the driver will accept, measured. Small-pulse compensation is applied only above this and never below it, so the injector is never asked for a pulse it cannot deliver.

items.name: injector_max_pulse_ms
items.description: Software pulse ceiling, always below the duty ceiling expressed as time. This is one of the two independent brakes on over-fuelling (the other is safety.injector_duty_max_pct); hazard H-05.

items.name: injector_dead_time_battery_slope
items.description: How dead time moves with battery voltage. A sagging pack opens the injector more slowly, so the pulse must widen; without this the engine goes lean every time the starter or a big injector pulse drags the rail down (test F4).

items.name: injector_battery_comp_pct_per_v
items.description: Additional pulse-width compensation per volt away from the nominal rail. Deliberately small: the dominant battery effect is dead time, not driver resistance, and over-compensating is how a crank-start transient floods.

items.name: injector_pressure_comp_pct_per_bar
items.description: Pulse-width correction per bar of deviation from the reference pressure. The physics is sqrt(P) for an orifice; this is the linearised, measured form of it, and a linear gain hides the fact that the true curve is a square root.

items.name: injector_small_pulse_comp_pct
items.description: Shortening or widening applied in the dead-time-dominated region only. Disabled while a fuel cut is active: compensation must never resurrect a cut event (FUEL-001 sec.5).

items.name: staged_split_fraction
items.description: Fraction of the demanded fuel mass delivered by the *primary* injector; the remainder goes to the secondary. Both are subject to the same min/max pulse, duty ceiling and fuel-cut gate - staged injection is a split, not an exemption.

items.name: staged_activate_primary_duty_pct
items.description: Activation predicate term. Above this, single injector flow would be outside the linear range the flow number was measured over, so the split turns on.

items.name: staged_activate_ect_c
items.description: Cold engines use large pulses; staged injection is normally inhibited until warm, because two small cold pulses are harder to model than one large one.

items.name: transient_tps_gain
items.description: Enrichment added per percentage point of *excess* throttle rate above the threshold. Bounded, decayed and logged; a term with no bound is a prohibited defect (FUEL-001 sec.6).

items.name: transient_tps_tau_ms
items.description: Decay time constant of the enrichment accumulator. Not a filter delay.

items.name: transient_map_gain
items.description: Pressure-based transient gain, used where throttle rate is a poor predictor - drive-by-wire, or a MAP sensor behind a plenum with poor resolution.

items.name: transient_tip_in_gain_pct
items.description: Discrete tip-in addition on a throttle opening above the threshold. Separate from the rate-based term so a tuner can take one out without losing the other.

items.name: transient_tip_out_gain_pct
items.description: Tip-out pulse *reduction*, toward -not-absolutely-zero: the pulse is never driven below the minimum pulse by this term, and a fuel cut always wins.

items.name: wall_wet_tau_ms
items.description: Time constant of the wall-wetting film state variable. Register UNK-FW-007 - the film model form for a motorcycle injector is literature only and has not been measured on this engine.

items.name: target_lambda_bias
items.description: Additive bias on the target lambda, clamped by the lambda target bias limits. Separate from the closed-loop correction so a tuner can see the commanded target and the measured correction as two different numbers in a log.

items.name: target_lambda_cold_ect_c
items.description: Engine temperature below which the target lambda is enriched for cold running. A failed ECT sensor therefore cannot command an absurdly rich mixture, because the enrichment is bounded by cold_ect_c and cold_gain together.

items.name: target_lambda_cold_gain
items.description: Strength of cold enrichment as a fraction of the temperature distance below cold_ect_c. Capped at 0.5, so cold enrichment can at most halve the target lambda and never invert it.

items.name: target_lambda_baro_gain
items.description: Altitude compensation gain: the factor applied per 100 kPa of barometric deficit. 1.0 disables it, which is the correct setting when the ECU has learned its baro at key-on from a MAP sensor on the manifold.

items.name: wall_wet_max_pct
items.description: Bounded film mass, so a wet port cannot justify an unbounded pulse.

items.name: decel_cut_tps_pct
items.description: Closed-throttle threshold for the overrun fuel cut. The cut decision is made once, in a dedicated arbiter, and applied as a hard gate at the output stage after every other calculation (FUEL-001 sec.7).

items.name: decel_cut_map_kpa
items.description: Manifold threshold for the overrun cut. TPS alone is a poor overrun detector under drive-by-wire or with a sloppy linkage, so pressure is the second term.

items.name: decel_cut_reintro_rpm
items.description: Reintroduction requires rpm above this AND the hysteresis timer elapsed AND throttle or MAP above the threshold AND the clutch/gear condition satisfied - all four, not any one.

items.name: decel_cut_hysteresis_ms
items.description: Without hysteresis a chattering throttle re-opens and closes the injector every few cycles, which is how a saturated driver dies.

items.name: enrichment_accumulator_max_pct
items.description: Ceiling on the single enrichment accumulator. There is exactly one accumulator; independent enrichers must not be able to stack silently (FUEL-001 sec.6).

items.name: ve_table
items.description: Volumetric efficiency, 0..200 %, against rpm and manifold pressure. The axis values come from companion dimension items so a 2-cylinder build drives the same allocation over a narrower range. Interpolated bilinearly with axis monotonicity validated; a non-monotonic axis is refused at write time.

items.name: target_lambda_table
items.description: Target lambda against rpm and load. The commanded value is this table times the ethanol blend correction, times the mode target, plus the temperature correction and the bounded closed-loop bias - in that order, and finally clamped by the lean safety envelope (hazard H-05 / test F17).

items.name: fuel_strategy
items.description: Load estimator. Every strategy reports (value, source, confidence) and a strategy whose sensor is invalid fails to a declared fallback recorded in the correction vector - it never silently produces a number (FUEL-001 sec.2).

items.name: fuel_hybrid_map_weight
items.description: Weight on the MAP term in hybrid. A named, calibrated, logged term - the point of listing it separately is that it is not hidden inside an average.

items.name: learner_enabled
items.description: 4D long-term learner. Off by default: convergence and drift in traffic are unproven for this engine, and a self-inflicted lean is worse than a static error. Register UNK-FW-011.

items.name: learner_trim_max_pct
items.description: Absolute bound on any learned trim. On reaching it the cell freezes and raises a DTC; it never continues to walk (test F16).

items.name: learner_drift_alarm_pct
items.description: If the *average* learned trim across the table exceeds this, the ECU raises a drift alarm: that pattern indicates a sensor or fuel problem, not a calibration that wants updating.

items.name: ve_table_rpm_axis
items.description: rpm breakpoints for ve_table: 16 of them, strictly increasing. These are the coordinates the table is interpolated along, and they live in the calibration rather than in the firmware so a tuner can put the resolution where the engine actually spends its time - at idle, usually, rather than spread evenly across a range it never visits.

items.name: ve_table_map_kpa_axis
items.description: map_kpa breakpoints for ve_table: 16 of them, strictly increasing. These are the coordinates the table is interpolated along, and they live in the calibration rather than in the firmware so a tuner can put the resolution where the engine actually spends its time - at idle, usually, rather than spread evenly across a range it never visits.

items.name: target_lambda_table_rpm_axis
items.description: rpm breakpoints for target_lambda_table: 8 of them, strictly increasing. These are the coordinates the table is interpolated along, and they live in the calibration rather than in the firmware so a tuner can put the resolution where the engine actually spends its time - at idle, usually, rather than spread evenly across a range it never visits.

items.name: ignition_base_table
items.description: Base advance in crank degrees BTDC. Every correction is added to this and the sum is clamped by the hard safety envelope *last*, so no combination of corrections and user trim can push past it (hazard H-02, test I12).

items.name: dwell_table
items.description: Commanded dwell in ms against battery voltage and rpm. The physics underneath is primary - primary inductance, resistance, target current - but the shipped default is unverified until it is measured with a current probe on a real coil. Register UNK-GT-006.

items.name: dwell_min_ms
items.description: Software floor. Below this a coil does not reach primary current and there is no spark at all, so commanding less wastes the event.

items.name: dwell_max_ms
items.description: Software ceiling. Must not exceed the hardware-enforced value in hardware.ignition_max_dwell_ms, and the two are independent by design: a hung CPU must still be unable to cook a coil.

items.name: coil_on_timeout_ms
items.description: Independent watchdog on total coil-on time, separate from the dwell control logic and from the main loop. Sync loss during dwell de-energises the coil immediately; no stored energy is left in it (test I6).

items.name: ignition_cyl0_trim_deg
items.description: Per-cylinder timing trim, applied before the safety clamp. A parallel twin with a shared exhaust can genuinely need a split; a four with equal lengths must be left at zero rather than trimmed by feel.

items.name: ignition_high_rpm_retard
items.description: Retard applied per 1000 rpm above the point the available spark energy stops keeping up. Rather than being hidden in the map, it is a named term in the correction vector.

items.name: ignition_iat_correction_deg
items.description: Timing correction at the hot end of the intake-air range; normally negative, because warm dense charge burns faster. The magnitude is engine-specific.

items.name: ignition_ect_correction_deg
items.description: Timing correction at the hot end of the coolant range; usually negative, and normally larger in magnitude than the IAT term because it reflects real knock tendency rather than charge density.

items.name: ignition_battery_retard_below_v
items.description: Battery voltage below which the retard policy engages.

items.name: ignition_battery_retard_deg
items.description: Retard applied at that voltage. Low voltage means the coil is not reaching primary current, so the honest response is less timing, not more (test I5).

items.name: ignition_user_trim_max_deg
items.description: Bound on the per-cell user trim, so a trim cannot be used to smuggle advance past the safety envelope by another route.

items.name: ignition_strategy
items.description: Which correction sources are allowed to modify the base map. static_table is what a dyno session wants: it is reproducible, because nothing is adapting under the measurement.

items.name: spark_duration_min_us
items.description: Shortest spark-duration feedback pulse treated as a real spark event. This is what turns "we commanded a spark" into "a spark was observed"; a mismatch raises a DTC instead of being invisible.

items.name: spark_duration_max_us
items.description: Upper bound of a plausible spark event; beyond it the feedback is noise.

items.name: narrowband_switch_threshold_v
items.description: Switching voltage of a narrowband sensor. The ECU uses it for a switching period and a duty-based average only; a narrowband sensor is *never* treated as a wide-range AFR readout. Register UNK-GT-010.

items.name: narrowband_dwell_time_ms
items.description: Minimum time at each state before the sensor is considered to have switched. Without it a noisy edge produces a nonsense average lambda.

items.name: wideband_controller_type
items.description: How lambda is obtained. The native path requires the CJ125 to be physically present (CAP_WIDEBAND); without it no wideband feature is offered at all rather than being simulated (IOM-001 sec.6).

items.name: wideband_heater_enabled
items.description: Wideband heater. Off by default: it is a large continuous load on a motorcycle charging system, and it must be actively asked for.

items.name: wideband_heater_duty_pct
items.description: Heater duty. High enough to reach the sensor's operating temperature, low enough not to cook it; a hot LSU destroys itself, so this is a bounded value and not a "full on".

items.name: wideband_warmup_timeout_ms
items.description: Time allowed for the sensor to be considered ready. Before it expires, closed loop is not entered at all - an unheated LSU reports confidently and wrongly.

items.name: lambda_target_bias_min
items.description: Most negative bias the long-term learner may apply to the target. A learner that can walk the mixture arbitrarily is a self-inflicted lean, so the bias is bounded per cell, per cylinder and globally.

items.name: lambda_target_bias_max
items.description: Most positive bias, richer than the table value. A0 asymmetric on purpose: drifting rich is recoverable in traffic, drifting lean is not.

items.name: lambda_closed_loop_gain
items.description: Proportional correction per unit lambda error. The loop bandwidth is deliberately limited: the time constant must be much longer than the sensor response and much shorter than the transient time constant. A controller is never shipped with an unmeasured gain (UNK-FW-010).

items.name: lambda_closed_loop_timeout_ms
items.description: A controller that reports "sensor not ready" is invalid and the loop is not entered; a controller that stops reporting entirely times out here into a declared fallback rather than a held value.

items.name: lambda_cyl0_trim_pct
items.description: Per-cylinder fuelling trim. Only meaningful where a per-cylinder channel physically exists; the validator refuses this feature beyond hardware_lambda_channel_count, so a single common-exhaust sensor can never be made to look like four.

items.name: lambda_cyl0_trim_min
items.description: Hard lower bound on cylinder 0 trim, applied after every correction.

items.name: knock_enabled
items.description: Off by default because no knock sensor is known to be fitted on this engine. Knock detection is impossible without one, and the ECU must not pretend otherwise. Register UNK-FW-008.

items.name: knock_cyl0_window_center_deg
items.description: Crank angle after this cylinder's TDC at which its knock window is centred. The window is placed from the firing angle, not guessed, so a change of firing order moves it with it.

items.name: knock_cyl0_window_size_deg
items.description: Half-width is *not* implied: a wide window catches more knock and more noise, a narrow one misses a slow burn. The size is a calibration because the block's resonant frequency is (UNK-FW-008).

items.name: knock_filter_low_hz
items.description: Lower corner of the conditioning band-pass.

items.name: knock_filter_high_hz
items.description: Upper corner. The band is narrow on purpose: widening it admits combustion noise and mechanical ring, which then looks like knock everywhere.

items.name: knock_threshold
items.description: Envelope level counted as a knock event. It is referenced to the measured noise floor below, not to an absolute voltage, so a different mounting position does not invalidate it.

items.name: knock_noise_floor
items.description: Estimated noise floor of the conditioned signal. Without it a disconnected sensor masquerades as "no knock" - or as constant knock, depending on the noise. Both failure modes are damaging.

items.name: knock_retard_per_event_deg
items.description: Retard requested per detected event, accumulated per cylinder.

items.name: knock_max_total_retard_deg
items.description: Ceiling on accumulated retard. Beyond it the response escalates to a cut rather than continuing to retard into the engine.

items.name: knock_recovery_deg_per_s
items.description: Rate at which retard is released. Recovery is deliberately slow: snapping back to full advance the moment the signal quietens is how engines get hurt, because the knock that mattered is still ringing.

items.name: knock_escalation_2_retard_deg
items.description: Total retard at which persistent knock escalates to an ignition cut, a second stage beyond simple retard.

items.name: knock_escalation_3_events
items.description: Events within the window below which escalation escalates again, to shutdown.

items.name: knock_event_window_ms
items.description: Window over which knock events are counted for the escalation decision. A count without a window is meaningless - it would escalate on any total.

items.name: idle_strategy
items.description: How idle is controlled. Most parallel twins have no idle actuator at all and idle is ignition plus a bypass, so none is the honest default. Register UNK-GT-011.

items.name: idle_pwm_frequency_hz
items.description: PWM carrier for the idle valve. Above the audible band a valve that chatters is a symptom of too low a frequency or too little current.

items.name: idle_stepper_steps
items.description: Full-travel step count. A stepper commanded past its end stops silently and the calibration has no idea, so travel is a stated number.

items.name: idle_stepper_max_energised_ms
items.description: Maximum energised time before the stepper is de-energised and returned toward zero. A stepper that is commanded forever is a thermal event, not a convenience (ACT-001 sec.4, test A12).

items.name: idle_valve_duty_max_pct
items.description: Bound on idle air. A stuck-open idle valve floods the engine and floods the exhaust, so the ceiling is a calibration value with a reason, not a guess.

items.name: idle_dashpot_gain
items.description: Proportional gain of the air dashpot on rpm error. Terminology carried over from a carburettor because the physics is the same; it is a PID term, not a legacy artefact.

items.name: idle_antistall_rpm_drop
items.description: How far below the target the idle controller may let rpm fall before the anti-stall assist engages. This is the last defence against a stall in traffic, and it engages on rpm, never on a timer.

items.name: idle_antistall_torque_scale
items.description: Fraction of full authority available to the anti-stall assist. Bounded below one on purpose: a stall assist that can command full torque on a stationary engine is a rev limiter wearing a different name.

items.name: idle_antistall_hold_ms
items.description: Maximum time the assist may stay engaged. Every latching request has a maximum lifetime; a latch with no release path is a prohibited defect.

items.name: idle_exit_rpm
items.description: Hysteresis on idle entry/exit, so a rider feathering the throttle does not make the idle controller and the rider fight each other.

items.name: idle_open_loop_gain
items.description: Feed-forward term - a lookup of position against coolant temperature.

items.name: idle_closed_loop_gain
items.description: Integral authority on rpm error, per second. Kept low deliberately: an integral term large enough to react quickly is also large enough to hunt.

items.name: idle_enable_at_ect_c
items.description: Coolant temperature above which idle control takes over. Below it, cold start enrichment owns the mixture and an idle controller would fight it.

items.name: boost_target_table
items.description: Target manifold pressure in kPa absolute against rpm and load. Boost is a requesting subsystem, not an override: overboost protection outranks it in the torque manager (TQM-001 rank 10).

items.name: boost_closed_loop_enabled
items.description: Off by default. A naturally aspirated engine must not have a boost controller quietly commanding a solenoid, and closed loop with unmeasured gains is exactly the oscillation risk UNK-FW-010 is about.

items.name: boost_p_gain
items.description: Proportional gain, duty fraction per kPa of error. The stability margin must be measured in SIL/HIL before this loop is ever enabled.

items.name: boost_d_gain
items.description: Derivative term, left at zero: the measured signal is already noisy and the derivative amplifies exactly the part that is not information.

items.name: boost_integral_limit_pct
items.description: Anti-windup clamp on the integral term. A wound-up boost controller is a boost controller that overshoots the moment the limit releases.

items.name: boost_wastegate_min_duty_pct
items.description: Duty the controller may reduce to. A floor above zero models a wastegate that cannot fully close - a real and frequently overlooked mechanical fact.

items.name: boost_wastegate_max_duty_pct
items.description: Duty the controller may command. Left below 100 % so a failed solenoid does not become a stuck-open gate.

items.name: boost_open_loop_gain
items.description: Feed-forward from the target table before any feedback, so a step demand does not rely on the loop to find the level from scratch.

items.name: boost_overboost_limit_kpa
items.description: Boost-controller protection threshold: the emergency trip the boost subsystem takes, which must sit ABOVE the design maximum so a healthy closed loop never reaches it. safety.boost_max_kpa is the non-bypassable envelope below it.

items.name: boost_closed_loop_rpm_min
items.description: Below this rpm the loop is open: at low speed a small pressure error is a large mass error and the feedback is not informative.

items.name: boost_closed_loop_rpm_max
items.description: Upper end of the closed-loop band, where the valve starts to lag.

items.name: boost_solenoid_pwm_hz
items.description: Solenoid PWM carrier. Bounded duty, and the output is off on overboost, sync loss or a closed-loop fault (ACT-001 sec.6).

items.name: vvt_enabled
items.description: Off by default. The GT650 is an overhead-cam engine with no phaser, and enabling VVT on hardware that does not have it would be exactly the fabricated capability the product is required not to claim (IOM-001 sec.6).

items.name: vvt_target_table
items.description: Target phaser angle in crank degrees against rpm and load. Positive is advanced; the actual authority is limited by the actuator and verified by position feedback, never by this table alone.

items.name: vvt_min_duty_pct
items.description: Duty the controller may reduce to. A floor above zero keeps oil pressure to the phaser above the unlock threshold at high rpm.

items.name: vvt_max_duty_pct
items.description: Duty ceiling, held below 100 % so a failed solenoid is not a fully open phaser.

items.name: vvt_p_gain
items.description: Proportional gain, duty fraction per degree of position error.

items.name: vvt_integral_limit_pct
items.description: Anti-windup clamp, for the same reason as boost - a wound-up controller is a stored overshoot waiting for the moment the limit releases.

items.name: vvt_position_tolerance_deg
items.description: Position error beyond which closed loop stops integrating and raises a DTC. The point is to catch a phaser that is not following its command before the timing is silently wrong.

items.name: vvt_feedback_enabled
items.description: Whether a position sensor exists. Off means the controller is open loop and the ECU must say so in the capability frame rather than implying verification.

items.name: vvt_target_table_rpm_axis
items.description: rpm breakpoints for vvt_target_table: 8 of them, strictly increasing.
