items.name: flexfuel_enabled
items.description: Off by default: a motorcycle with no flex sensor has a fixed blend, set once in the engine group. Enabling this without a sensor would make the ECU blend from noise.

items.name: flexfuel_sensor_type
items.description: How the ethanol fraction is obtained. A CAN source must have an explicit timeout and a defined fallback, or a dead adapter would freeze the blend.

items.name: flexfuel_cold_start_enrich_pct
items.description: Cold-start enrichment at full ethanol. Ethanol needs more mixture to reach the same lambda target, and on top of that its higher charge temperature changes how that mixture burns cold.

items.name: flexfuel_ignition_blend_deg
items.description: Timing change at full ethanol. Ethanol's higher charge temperature and latent heat mean *more* advance is usually needed, not less - the opposite of the instinct imported from gasoline, and the reason this is a calibration with a sign rather than a fixed rule.

items.name: flexfuel_ignition_blend_max_deg
items.description: Ceiling on the ignition blend term, so a misreading blend cannot move timing without limit.

items.name: flexfuel_min_ethanol_fraction
items.description: Lowest fraction accepted from the sensor. Below this the reading is treated as a fault rather than blended, because a 0 % floor is where a disconnected sensor would otherwise land.

items.name: flexfuel_max_ethanol_fraction
items.description: Highest fraction accepted. Deliberately below 1.0 by default: a genuine E100 fill is rare enough on a motorcycle that being told about it is more useful than silently running a blend the calibration was never set up for.

items.name: flexfuel_switch_hysteresis_frac
items.description: Hysteresis on switching the *active* blend between two adjacent calibrated points, so a signal hovering at a boundary does not dither the whole model.

items.name: flexfuel_invalid_action
items.description: What happens when the blend sensor fails. Reverting to the fixed blend in the engine group is the default, because a *wrong* blend is a persistent fuelling error while a *stale* one is at least visible.

items.name: gear_ratio_1
items.description: Transmission ratios. These are facts about the gearbox, not tuning choices, so they are only as good as the service manual - and the GT650 gearbox ratio is not published. A wrong ratio does not hurt the engine; it makes gear-derived speed, shift scheduling, launch and the pit limiter all quietly wrong.

items.name: primary_ratio
items.description: Primary reduction, between crank and gearbox input. live_edit false.

items.name: gear_ratio_count
items.description: Number of forward ratios this configuration declares. The remaining gear_ratio_* items stay in the image but are not used, which keeps ids stable if a different gearbox is configured. live_edit false.

items.name: tyre_circumference_m
items.description: Rolling circumference of the driven tyre. Together with the ratios this is what turns engine rpm into road speed, and it is the second half of the kinematic consistency check against the wheel-speed sensor (SENS-001 sec.8).

items.name: reverse_detection_enabled
items.description: Most motorcycles have no reverse. It stays off until a gear sensor or a kinematic derivation exists, and neither is known for this bike. Register UNK-GT-015.

items.name: reverse_speed_threshold_kph
items.description: Below this road speed, rpm and wheel speed disagreeing in the reverse direction is treated as reverse. Small because a false positive at speed means an unintended launch-direction command.

items.name: gear_strategy_table
items.description: Per-gear torque scale, percent, against gear and rpm. This is a *request*, not a command: it enters the torque manager as a requester and loses to anything protective, exactly like every other feature.

items.name: gear_strategy_table_gear_axis
items.description: gear breakpoints for gear_strategy_table: 8 of them, strictly increasing. These are the coordinates the table is interpolated along, and they live in the calibration rather than in the firmware so a tuner can put the resolution where the engine actually spends its time - at idle, usually, rather than spread evenly across a range it never visits.

items.name: gear_strategy_table_rpm_axis
items.description: rpm breakpoints for gear_strategy_table: 8 of them, strictly increasing. These are the coordinates the table is interpolated along, and they live in the calibration rather than in the firmware so a tuner can put the resolution where the engine actually spends its time - at idle, usually, rather than spread evenly across a range it never visits.

items.name: torque_scale_min
items.description: Lowest authority a requester may reduce to. 0.0 is a cut; a product that cannot express a cut through the same path it uses for a 5 % reduction is a product with two paths to get the arbitration wrong.

items.name: torque_scale_max
items.description: Ceiling of the scale. It is 1.0 and it cannot exceed 1.0: arbitration scales *requests*, and there is no requester that may raise one above the base request (TQM-001 R4).

items.name: torque_reduction_step
items.description: Resolution of the emitted scale. Coarse steps make a continuous requester (traction) quantised, which shows up as a hunting driveline; too fine a step costs nothing but hides the fact that a "continuous" request is a sampled one.

items.name: retard_per_unit_torque_loss
items.description: Timing removed per unit of (1 - allowed_scale) when fuel has been cut. This is the retard_equivalent of TQM-001 sec.3, and it is explicitly *not* a guess: the relationship between advance and torque is engine-specific, so this number has to come from a measured torque curve, not from a rule of thumb.

items.name: retard_equivalent_max_deg
items.description: Ceiling on the retard_equivalent term. A fully cut fuel request must not also remove unbounded spark, or a rev limiter would command a total loss of combustion rather than a controlled one.

items.name: requester_enable_bits
items.description: Which requesters are wired into the arbiter, in the fixed rank order of TQM-001 R2. This is an *enable* mask, not a reordering: clearing a bit removes a requester, and no arrangement of these bits can change which requester wins. Bit 0 is the strongest reduction.

items.name: torque_latch_max_ms
items.description: Maximum lifetime of any latching request (TQM-001 R7). A latch with no release path is a prohibited defect - it is a slow brick in software form - so the bound is structural and applies to every requester at once.

items.name: torque_trace_enabled
items.description: Emit the arbitration trace: winning requester, applied scale, ignition request, fuel request. Traceability is the difference between an arbitration table that is meaningful and one that is aspirational (R6, test TM9). On by default because it is cheap and it is the only way to explain a single cylinder's behaviour after the fact.

items.name: launch_enabled
items.description: Off by default: launch control also needs a clutch or shift switch, and neither is known to be fitted. Register UNK-GT-016.

items.name: launch_target_rpm
items.description: Engine speed held during a launch. It is a *request* through the torque manager, so a rev limiter or a knock event at that speed wins without any special case.

items.name: launch_retard_deg
items.description: Retard applied while the launch is engaged. Under load a launch develops far more torque than a cruise at the same rpm, and launching at cruise timing is how the first clutch bite destroys a clutch.

items.name: launch_torque_scale
items.description: Ceiling on the authority a launch may request.

items.name: launch_ramp_time_ms
items.description: Time to reach the launch authority. A step from idle to full launch torque shakes the bike and is how a rider loses it; a ramp is a calibration, not a safety limit.

items.name: launch_timeout_ms
items.description: Maximum time a launch may remain engaged. A launch control that never ends is a rev limiter with a worse personality.

items.name: launch_abort_torque_scale
items.description: Authority on abort - clutch dump, brake applied, or the timeout. The abort path is what makes a launch a bounded feature rather than a condition.

items.name: launch_wheelie_mitigation_enabled
items.description: Wheelie mitigation only if the hardware supports the required input. With no IMU and no fork-travel input there is nothing to mitigate with, and offering the feature anyway would be a fabricated capability.

items.name: launch_wheelie_front_lift_gain
items.description: Reduction per unit of front-lift signal, when such a signal exists.

items.name: launch_fuel_trim_pct
items.description: Small fuelling trim during a launch. Deliberately tiny: most launches want *less* mixture than cruise because of the heat soak, and a large trim is a flooding risk on a bike that is barely moving.

items.name: launch_min_speed_kph
items.description: Road speed below which a launch is not permitted to engage.

items.name: launch_max_boost_kpa
items.description: Boost ceiling during a launch. Drag starts can legitimately ask for more than street boost, and the safety limit still applies unchanged above this.

items.name: shift_strategy
items.description: What a quickshift actually removes. Fuel cut is the default because it is what a mechanical fuel-injected engine recovers from fastest; spark cut is gentler on the driveline but must never be allowed to overlap a traction cut.

items.name: shift_max_cut_ms
items.description: Duration-bounded cut. The shift is a requester with a bounded lifetime, so a shift that never completes cannot leave the engine without fuel.

items.name: shift_min_time_between_ms
items.description: Minimum time between two shifts. A bouncing switch or a noisy paddle must not be able to open a cut every cycle.

items.name: shift_recovery_torque_scale
items.description: Authority during shift recovery. Ramped back rather than returned at once, so the re-engagement does not arrive as a second torque step.

items.name: shift_blip_enabled
items.description: Auto-blip on downshift. Needs a clutch lever switch, which is not known to be fitted. Register UNK-GT-016.

items.name: shift_blip_torque_scale
items.description: Authority during the blip. A blip is a throttle-matching event; giving it full authority is a clutch dump with extra steps.

items.name: shift_min_rpm
items.description: Below this rpm a shift is ignored; there is nothing to gain.

items.name: shift_tps_threshold_pct
items.description: Minimum throttle opening for a shift to count as deliberate. Coasting downshifts are a different event with different consequences.

items.name: shift_release_timeout_ms
items.description: If the gear or clutch condition that ends the shift never arrives, this ends it. The re-enable predicate is bounded in time as well as in condition.

items.name: traction_enabled
items.description: Off by default: traction control needs front *and* rear wheel speed, and no ABS sensor is known to exist on this bike. Register UNK-GT-014. The GUI hides the workspace entirely when CAP_TRACTION is off.

items.name: traction_slip_target_pct
items.description: Allowed slip ratio difference, percent, between driven and reference wheel. The number itself is a rider-preference compromise between fast and stable.

items.name: traction_slip_ramp_pct_per_s
items.description: Slew rate on the target. A step target is a step torque demand, and a step torque demand on a rear tyre is a spin.

items.name: traction_gear_correction
items.description: Multiplier on the slip target in first gear, where slip is physically larger and the target has to be looser to be stable.

items.name: traction_speed_correction_kph
items.description: Speed at which the correction reaches full effect. Below it the target is tightened, because at walking pace a slip ratio is noise.

items.name: traction_rpm_correction
items.description: Multiplier on the slip target with engine speed, to account for the extra inertia the rear wheel has to work with.

items.name: traction_min_slip_to_act
items.description: Below this the controller does not act at all. Without it the loop chases sensor noise at zero slip and the rider feels an engine that is mysteriously hesitating.

items.name: traction_intervention_hold_ms
items.description: Minimum time the control stays engaged after an intervention, so it does not chatter on and off as the tyre oscillates across the target.

items.name: traction_gain
items.description: Authority per unit slip error; it becomes a torque-manager request.

items.name: traction_retard_max_deg
items.description: Ceiling on the retard the traction requester may add.

items.name: traction_min_speed_kph
items.description: Below this the controller is disabled. A two-wheel speed difference at 3 km/h is a speedometer discrepancy, not a slide.

items.name: traction_wheel_timeout_ms
items.description: Freshness limit on the wheel-speed sources. A stale wheel reading is worse than none: the controller would act confidently on a value from half a second ago.

items.name: engine_braking_enabled
items.description: Off by default. On a motorcycle with twin carburettors the engine brake is usually the rider's own right foot; enabling a fuel-cut-based engine brake changes the bike's character permanently, so it is opt-in.

items.name: ebt_retard_table
items.description: Retard on overrun against gear and rpm. Positive advances and negative retards, so the sign convention matches the rest of the ignition corrections and does not need its own explanation in a log.

items.name: ebt_fuel_cut_map_kpa
items.description: Manifold pressure below which overrun fuel cut applies. As with the decel cut, this is the *engine braking* threshold, which is deliberately tighter than the ordinary overrun cut.

items.name: ebt_min_rpm
items.description: Below this, engine braking is off: a lean mixture at low rpm is a stumble, not a brake, and a stumble under a closed throttle is how a bike gets dropped at a junction.

items.name: ebt_max_torque_scale
items.description: Floor on the allowed scale while the engine brake is active. Bounded above zero so a mid-corner downshift cannot command a total loss of drive.

items.name: ebt_recovery_tau_ms
items.description: Time constant for handing authority back on throttle return. Slow enough that releasing the throttle does not feel like a torque step.

items.name: ebt_retard_table_gear_axis
items.description: gear breakpoints for ebt_retard_table: 8 of them, strictly increasing. These are the coordinates the table is interpolated along, and they live in the calibration rather than in the firmware so a tuner can put the resolution where the engine actually spends its time - at idle, usually, rather than spread evenly across a range it never visits.

items.name: ebt_retard_table_rpm_axis
items.description: rpm breakpoints for ebt_retard_table: 8 of them, strictly increasing. These are the coordinates the table is interpolated along, and they live in the calibration rather than in the firmware so a tuner can put the resolution where the engine actually spends its time - at idle, usually, rather than spread evenly across a range it never visits.

items.name: pit_limiter_enabled
items.description: Off by default. A pit limiter that cannot be disengaged is a safety defect in itself, so the disengage path is defined and tested before the feature is offered at all (TQM-001 sec.5, test TM11).

items.name: pit_target_rpm
items.description: Speed target needs a wheel-speed source, which this bike may not have; the rpm target works without one and is the safer of the two.

items.name: pit_speed_hysteresis_kph
items.description: Hysteresis, so the limiter does not chatter on and off around the target as the bike accelerates through it in a straight line.

items.name: pit_gear_override_enabled
items.description: Use per-gear rpm limits instead of the single rpm target. Useful on a circuit where the same engine speed means different things in different gears, but it depends on knowing the gear.

items.name: pit_release_delay_ms
items.description: Minimum time between the cut ending and it being allowed to end again. The limiter owns its own cut, and this is the bound on that ownership.

items.name: pit_activation_switch_inverted
items.description: True when the pit switch is active-low. The polarity is explicit because a pit limiter wired to the wrong state is a limiter that engages in the pit.

items.name: modes_enabled
items.description: Which drive modes exist in this configuration. A mode selects a calibration *overlay*; it never selects a code path, and it can never change a hard safety limit, because those live in the base image (CAL-001 sec.3).

items.name: mode_default_load
items.description: Mode loaded on power-up, before the user chooses. Street is the default because it is the only mode that is safe to be in while the bike is being wheeled out of a workshop.

items.name: mode_count
items.description: Number of modes this build declares. It is a build-time count, not a tuning choice, and it is why it cannot be changed while the engine runs. live_edit false.

items.name: mode_switch_live
items.description: Whether a mode change may be applied while the engine is running. A mode switch is a small validated transaction that takes effect at a defined point in the cycle, never part way through an injection or a spark event.

items.name: mode_switch_coast_ms
items.description: Minimum time between two mode changes. Modes select overlays, and a driver toggling between them mid-corner would otherwise get an overlay per cycle - a step change in fuelling and timing with no physical event behind it.

items.name: rpm_limit
items.description: Hard rev limit. Above it there is no spark and no fuel. This is the *ECU* limit; the trigger subsystem's overspeed_period_us is a separate, faster and hardware-backed path for the case where the CPU is not keeping up (H-09).

items.name: rpm_hysteresis
items.description: Speed the limit releases at. Without hysteresis the limiter chatters on and off at the limit, and every cycle of that chatter is a fuelling transient.

items.name: overspeed_rpm
items.description: Instantaneous overspeed, above which a fault is declared and outputs are inhibited without waiting for the limit. The gap between this and rpm_limit is the overshoot the limiter is allowed; it must exceed the measured scheduling error, which is not yet known (UNK-FW-002/003).

items.name: lean_lambda_limit
items.description: Leanest lambda the engine may be commanded to run at. This cuts and limits; it does not merely warn. The commanded target and the long-term learner bias are both clamped by it, so a bad day cannot walk the mixture lean (test F17).

items.name: rich_lambda_limit
items.description: Richest lambda permitted. A rich limit matters because over-fuelling is what destroys catalytic converters and what leaves a hot pipe that backfires on shutdown (H-05).

items.name: ect_max_c
items.description: Coolant over-temperature limit. The action escalates retard, then limits, then cuts; the escalation ladder is a safety group decision, not a feature one, because a mode must not be able to soften it (H-07, TM12).

items.name: iat_max_c
items.description: Charge-air temperature limit. Bound high because this is a *charge* sensor and genuinely hot air is survivable; it exists to catch a failed IAT that reports ambient forever and so disables every heat-based protection.

items.name: oil_pressure_min_bar
items.description: Minimum oil pressure. A latching cut with recovery hysteresis, not a warning: a motorcycle that has lost oil pressure is a few seconds from a seized engine and a rider who does not know (H-08). Register UNK-GT-018.

items.name: oil_pressure_recovery_bar
items.description: Pressure at which a latched oil cut is released. Above oil_pressure_min_bar by design: releasing at the trip point makes the ECU hunt across its own limit and the rider ride an engine that keeps cutting.

items.name: oil_temp_max_c
items.description: Oil over-temperature limit; derates before coolant does on most engines.

items.name: egt_max_c
items.description: Exhaust temperature limit. The single most consequential *unmeasured* number in this file: it is engine-, cylinder- and probe-specific, and it is the limit that stands between a lean condition and a melted exhaust valve. Register UNK-GT-006 for the coil and EGT probe placement is equally unknown.

items.name: battery_min_v
items.description: Under-voltage limit. Below it the coils cannot reach primary current, so the honest response is to retard and derate rather than to keep commanding spark the hardware cannot deliver.

items.name: battery_max_v
items.description: Over-voltage limit, from a failed regulator or a jump-start with the wrong battery. The ECU should refuse to run rather than let 18 V reach the analogue front end.

items.name: fuel_pressure_min_bar
items.description: Minimum rail pressure. A pressure drop is compensated *and* limited: the compensation corrects the metering, the limit stops an engine that is being fed by a dying pump. Register UNK-GT-005.

items.name: injector_duty_max_pct
items.description: ECU-side injector duty ceiling, independent of the hardware ceiling in hardware.injector_max_duty_pct. Two limits in two places is not redundancy for its own sake: the hardware one survives a wedged CPU, this one can be lowered by engineering mode per engine.

items.name: dwell_max
items.description: Safety ceiling on commanded dwell. The hardware max-dwell timer is the independent enforcement that survives a hung CPU (H-03, test I3); this value must stay at or below it, and the validator refuses a configuration where it does not.

items.name: boost_max_kpa
items.description: Non-bypassable overboost limit. A boost target above it is refused at validation time rather than clamped at runtime, so the mistake is visible in the tuner instead of hidden (H-19).

items.name: sync_loss_action
items.description: What loss of crank synchronisation does. The default is a request to cut, because without phase the ECU cannot know which cylinder is on its exhaust stroke, and a fuelling or spark event at the wrong phase is exactly H-01. Values are ordered from "carry on and log" to "latched shutdown".

items.name: action_level
items.description: The escalation ladder used when a limit is exceeded. The default is RETARD because a mild over-temperature or a single knock event should not stop a motorcycle mid-corner; the ladder exists so that persistence escalates automatically rather than relying on the rider noticing.

items.name: oil_cut_timeout_ms
items.description: Maximum lifetime of the latching oil cut. Every latch has a bound: a latch with no release path is a slow brick in software form (TQM-001 R7).

items.name: lean_cut_hold_ms
items.description: How long a lean excursion must persist before the cut latches. Short enough that a transient cannot be ridden through, long enough that a single noisy wideband frame does not stop the engine.

items.name: sensor_fallback_speed_limit_kph
items.description: Road speed above which a load-sensor failure escalates from a limp to a reduced-authority state. The philosophy in SC-001 sec.4 is that losing a comfort function must not stop a motorcycle mid-corner - but it must also not be running full authority on a guess at 100 km/h.

items.name: max_fuel_pressure_bar
items.description: Upper rail-pressure limit. A stuck regulator would otherwise push the injectors past every point of their flow curve and flood the engine.

items.name: can_bitrate
items.description: Nominal CAN rate. Persisted per project. 500 kbit/s is the common choice on modern motorcycles; the exact controller count on the chosen part is still open (UNK-REF-005).

items.name: can_db_default_timeout_ms
items.description: Default signal timeout applied to a new CAN database entry. A CAN frame may only be an input to the control loop if it has an explicit timeout, a fallback value and a validity flag - so the default is generous but finite.

items.name: can_db_default_min_raw
items.description: Default raw validity window of a new signal. Wide by default, because a narrow default silently rejects a legitimate signal from an adapter with a different scaling.

items.name: can_db_auto_apply_on_connect
items.description: Off by default: silently replacing a validated database on every connect makes it impossible to tell which database the engine is currently running against.

items.name: protocol_version
items.description: Wire protocol version, major packed in the high byte. A minor bump is backward compatible; a major bump is negotiated and never guessed (PROTO-001 sec.1). Derived from the firmware build.

items.name: session_timeout_ms
items.description: Bounded session lifetime. An expired session cannot write. Losing the session does not disturb the running engine, which is the behaviour that makes a dropped Wi-Fi link harmless (test PR8).

items.name: session_command_budget
items.description: Commands a session may issue before re-authentication. The budget exists so that a stolen-but-unfinished session is bounded in time as well as in privilege.

items.name: signed_tune_policy
items.description: How the ECU treats a tune with no valid RACCOON signature. This is a three-state trust model, and the middle state is a deliberate product decision, not a compromise: the release key signs firmware and *reference* configurations, but a third-party tuner who bought the product legitimately cannot obtain that key, so forcing every tune through it would make every legitimate tune permanently untrusted. Instead an unsigned tune is written only to the inactive slot, can never auto-activate, cannot arm until it is explicitly acknowledged with a valid session, and is labelled UNTRUSTED in every view *and in the log header* so a log can never misrepresent its own provenance. There is no public precedent for this, so the design has to stand on internal review alone (UNK-REF-006).

items.name: engineering_mode_enabled
items.description: Whether engineering mode exists at all in this build. On by default, and conspicuously so: a build where it *cannot* be enabled is a build whose diagnostics and bench procedures are one mistake away from being unrecoverable. It still requires an authenticated ENGINEER credential and every action it permits is audited.

items.name: engineering_mode_timeout_ms
items.description: Engineering mode expires on its own. It does not persist because someone enabled it once on a bench and never went back.

items.name: audit_log_enabled
items.description: Signed audit log of every privileged action - who, what, when, outcome, plus a monotonic counter - surviving power cycles and tamper-evident. Required by SEC-001 sec.6 and test SEC-11.

items.name: audit_log_entries
items.description: Retained audit entries. It is a ring: when it wraps, the fact that it wrapped is itself recorded, so a full log is never silently mistaken for a quiet one.

items.name: wireless_enabled
items.description: The ESP32-S3 wireless transport. Off by default, and it should stay a workshop and paddock tool: it is a *transport*, not a privilege. If the radio is absent the ECU behaves identically, and Wi-Fi association latency is unmeasured (UNK-SW-007).

items.name: wifi_tx_power_dbm
items.source_ref: ESP32-S3 datasheet (2.4 GHz 1T1R, up to +19.5 dBm)
items.description: Transmit power. It is bounded rather than pinned at maximum: +20 dBm from a pocket of metal in a fairing is both a EMC liability and a battery cost (355 mA at full power).

items.name: wifi_channel
items.description: Fixed 2.4 GHz channel. Fixed rather than scanned: a tuner that has to find the ECU on a congested band at a track is a tuner who cannot download a log before the session starts.

items.name: wifi_max_clients
items.description: Simultaneous stations. Small on purpose: every client is a live path to a calibration write, and the number is not a performance knob.

items.name: wireless_connect_timeout_ms
items.description: Association timeout before the transport is declared unavailable. Bounded so a dead AP cannot leave the transport layer spinning.

items.name: protocol_max_payload
items.description: Per-transport payload ceiling: 4096 for USB, 8 for CAN, 64 for CAN-FD. A larger payload is fragmented with a bounded fragment count and times out. Derived from the transport.

items.name: log_trigger_enabled
items.description: Per-tooth trigger log: tooth timestamps, periods, accepted flag, reason for rejection. This is the only rate that can show a decoder that is losing sync without the engine misfiring.

items.name: log_trigger_rate_hz
items.description: Nominal ceiling on the trigger group's sample rate. The group is really per-tooth, so this is a bound for admission, not a request for a fixed rate.

items.name: log_fast_enabled
items.description: Combustion-domain signals - knock envelope, spark current, crank angle.

items.name: log_core_enabled
items.description: The main tuning dataset - rpm, tps, map, lambda, injection ms, ignition deg, dwell and the whole correction vector. On by default because this is the record most logs are actually wanted for.

items.name: log_throughput_ceiling_kb_s
items.description: Total throughput ceiling across every group. A requested set that exceeds it is *refused with an explanation*, never silently degraded (test L7). The ceiling is meant to be measured against the real medium, which has not been selected yet - Register UNK-HW-009.

items.name: log_ring_buffer_s
items.description: RAM ring that absorbs burst rates. If the medium cannot keep up, the oldest data is dropped and the drop is recorded in the file header - a log that is quietly truncated is worse than a short one, because it looks complete.

items.name: log_event_enabled
items.description: Sparse event records - sync loss and gain, knock escalation, over-temperature, lean, overboost, rev limit, launch, shift, traction, sensor fault, watchdog, reset, brownout, calibration error. Pushed live as well as written, so a fault appears in the GUI *while it happens* rather than at the end of the session.

items.name: log_trigger_log_enabled
items.description: The dense trigger log in its own format, retained in a RAM ring and drained to storage. It is what the trigger oscilloscope in the GUI renders with the decoder state overlaid.

items.name: log_map_trace_enabled
items.description: Record the *active* table cell - id, row, col, value and interpolation fractions - with every sample group. It costs a few bytes per sample and it is the single most useful feature for answering "why did the engine do that" (LOG-001 sec.5, test L8).

items.name: log_freeze_frame_enabled
items.description: On a DTC, snapshot a CORE plus SLOW frame and the trigger-log window around the event, and store it with the code. Without it a fault is only explicable by the rider's memory.

items.name: log_channel_count_max
items.description: Upper bound on the channel count. Bounded at read time as well as at write time: a log file is fixed-size records with no unbounded channel count, so a malformed header cannot make a reader allocate.

items.name: injection_strategy
items.description: Injection firing mode. Sequential requires a valid cylinder phase source (cam sync, or a crank gap that fixes the 720 degree cycle); without one the ECU refuses to arm, because injecting into an exhaust stroke destroys an engine.

items.name: lambda_strategy
items.description: Lambda strategy. Narrowband is explicitly NOT treated as a wide-range AFR measurement (FUEL_SPEC section 8); native wideband requires a physically present CJ125 plus LSU 4.9 pair (CAP_WIDEBAND).

items.name: dbw_strategy
items.description: Electronic throttle. A cable throttle is NOT electronically controllable and must never be presented as DBW; without the pedal, motor and dual-channel redundancy hardware this stays 'off' (spec section 38, 44).

items.name: shift_request_source
items.description: What tells the ECU a shift is wanted. Flat shift and auto-blip are impossible without a request source; the ECU does not invent one (spec section 43, 44).

items.name: lambda_channel_count
items.description: Physically fitted lambda channels. Per-cylinder lambda is only claimed when a channel exists per cylinder; a single common-exhaust sensor is never demultiplexed into per-cylinder values without a validated methodology (FUEL_SPEC section 8, UNK-FW-009).

items.name: knock_sensor_count
items.description: Physically fitted knock sensors. No sensor means no knock claim, ever (spec section 34).

items.name: wheel_speed_channel_count
items.description: Fitted wheel speed channels. Traction control needs both axles to compute slip; one channel is enough for speed alone (spec section 45).

items.name: pedal_channel_count
items.description: Pedal position channels. DBW requires two for redundancy.

items.name: throttle_channel_count
items.description: Throttle position channels. Two are required for DBW plausibility; one is normal for a cable throttle (spec section 17).

items.name: clutch_switch_present
items.description: A clutch lever switch is fitted. Used for launch, flat shift and rev matching (spec section 43).

items.name: ignition_hard_min_deg
items.description: Lower bound of the hard ignition envelope. The final commanded advance is clamped into [ignition_hard_min_deg, ignition_hard_max_deg] AFTER every correction and every user trim, so no combination of trims can exceed it (spec section 31, CALIBRATION_SPEC section 110). Engineering mode may only narrow this envelope, never widen it.

items.name: ignition_hard_max_deg
items.description: Upper bound of the hard ignition envelope. See ignition_hard_min_deg.

items.name: cam_phase_verified
items.description: Set by the bench TDC procedure or the GUI TDC tool, never by the tuner, once the cam reference edge has been observed at a known TDC. The arming gate requires this for sequential injection and for the STROKE_DIRECTION item (spec section 98, GT650-001 section 4). Register UNK-GT-002, UNK-GT-003.

items.name: tdc_verified
items.description: Set once the timing light agrees with the ECU's reported crank angle at a known RPM. Until this is set, the configuration is not armable: a wrong trigger angle is the single most damaging miscalibration in the product (spec section 98). Register UNK-GT-001.

items.name: kill_switch_present
items.description: A kill switch is fitted. Engine control must not arm while it is active.

items.name: kill_switch_active_high
items.description: Which level means 'kill asserted'. A broken wire on a normally-closed kill circuit must present as 'engine may run', so the polarity is an explicit calibration rather than a default guess (SENSOR_SPEC section 5).

items.name: kill_switch_fault_behaviour
items.description: What a broken or missing kill-switch signal does. 'ignore' is refused by the schema rules: a build that cannot tell whether the rider asked to stop is unsafe.

items.name: brake_switch_present
items.description: A brake input is fitted. Used as a traction-control reference and to inhibit rev matching and the pit limiter (spec section 45, 47).

items.name: brake_switch_active_high
items.description: Which level means 'brake applied'.

items.name: side_stand_present
items.description: A side-stand switch is fitted. Usually retained by the OEM ECU; the RACCOON input exists so the tuner can see its state in logs and diagnostics.

items.name: side_stand_active_high
items.description: Which level means 'stand down'.

items.name: launch_button_present
items.description: A launch button is fitted. Without one, launch control has no request source.

items.name: launch_button_active_high
items.description: Which level means 'launch requested'.

items.name: pit_switch_present
items.description: A pit-lane switch is fitted (spec section 47).

items.name: pit_switch_active_high
items.description: Which level means 'pit limiter armed'.

items.name: switch_debounce_ms
items.description: Shared debounce window for the switch inputs. A real filter with a bounded window, not a single sample (SENSOR_SPEC section 5).

items.name: switch_timeout_ms
items.description: No-transition timeout for switch inputs. A signal that never changes for this long is reported stale; it is never silently treated as valid.

rules.name: ignition_table_within_envelope
rules.text: ignition_base_table inside the hard ignition envelope

rules.name: sequential_requires_cam
rules.text: sequential injection requires a cam source

rules.name: dbw_requires_dual_channel
rules.text: dbw_strategy != off implies 2 pedal and 2 throttle channels

rules.name: modes_bitfield_covers_all
rules.text: modes_enabled declares at least 10 bits for the 10 spec modes

rules.name: unverified_safety_not_sourced
rules.text: UNVERIFIED safety items carry no source_ref

rules.name: axis_breakpoints_increase
rules.text: axis breakpoints must strictly increase; a repeated or inverted pair makes the table it belongs to unsearchable, so the lookup returns a value from whichever cell it happened to land in
